_comment: Questions are grouped onto screens. A screen is a tight cluster asked together - one question per screen produced roughly 35 screens for a single case, which is where answer quality falls off. Free text is reserved for the handful of things a picker genuinely cannot capture: the task, the sequence, and why it happened.

stages.title: Case framing
stages.intro: A few facts so the wizard asks the right questions. Most are already on the I&I form - pick the same values here.

stages.title: Task and setting
stages.intro: What was being done, under what method, with what equipment.

stages.title: What happened
stages.intro: Before, during and after. These are the details a reviewer cannot get anywhere else.

stages.title: Mechanism
stages.intro: The physical detail: forces, distances, and where on the body the force landed.

stages.title: Contributing conditions
stages.intro: You are not doing the root cause analysis here. You are recording what a reviewer needs to start one.

stages.title: Immediate response
stages.intro: What was done at the scene, and who was told.

stages.title: Form cross-check
stages.intro: These live in structured fields on the form. Nothing here enters the description text.

stages.title: Review and copy
stages.intro: The composed description, checked against the six things reviewers most often find missing.

screens.title: What kind of case is this?
screens.intro: These four choices decide which questions you get. They are all on the form already.

screens.title: The sequence of events
screens.intro: Three separate moments. Answer them separately - one blob will not do.

questions.prompt: How did this case arise?
questions.help: The most important choice here. It changes the whole question set.
questions.why: Strain and sprain descriptions average 45 to 132 characters against 404 for recordables, mostly because the acute-event story does not fit them, so people write nothing. Picking the right pattern gets you a question set that does fit.

questions.prompt: Injury or illness?
Accident type
questions.help: Decides which mechanism questions you get.

questions.prompt: Principal body part
Role of the person involved
questions.help: The description will say the role, never a name.
questions.why: The form states plainly that no names or personal details go in this field, because the description is surfaced in emails and generic reports. The role keeps the text useful without identifying anyone.

questions.prompt: How did it come to light?
Was equipment, a tool or a machine involved?
questions.help: Yes if anything was being used, serviced, or moving nearby.
questions.why: Equipment detail is missing from 87.3 percent of past descriptions.

questions.prompt: Was something being lifted, carried or handled?
questions.help: Yes for anything held or moved by hand, including tools and parts.

questions.prompt: What was the person doing?
questions.help: Operational terms, not a job title. What their hands were actually doing.
questions.why: 73.5 percent of past descriptions never state the activity. Without it a reviewer cannot tell whether this was routine work, a recovery from a fault, or something nobody should have been doing.
questions.placeholder: Example: clearing a jammed carton from the infeed conveyor at station 4
examples: Clearing a jammed carton from the infeed conveyor at station 4
Changing the blade on the manual guillotine during a size changeover
Loading 40 pound resin bags from a pallet onto the mixer platform
Walking from the tool crib back to the line carrying a torque wrench

signals.message: That names a thing but not an action. What was the person doing to it?
signals.example: Instead of conveyor jam, write clearing a jammed carton from the conveyor guard opening.

questions.prompt: What stage of the task?
questions.help: Injuries cluster in setup, teardown and troubleshooting rather than steady running.

questions.prompt: Why was it being done right then?
questions.help: The reason often explains the shortcut.
questions.why: A jam cleared under production pressure is a different case from the same jam cleared during planned downtime. This is frequently where the cause sits.

questions.prompt: What written method covered this task?
questions.help: The document number if you know it. If there is genuinely none, say so - that is a real finding.
questions.why: 77.6 percent of past descriptions never mention a procedure. Whether one existed, and whether it was followed, is usually the first thing a reviewer asks.
questions.placeholder: SW-114, or: no written procedure exists
examples: SW-114 Conveyor Jam Clearing rev C
No written procedure exists for this task

signals.message: Give a document identifier, or state plainly that no written procedure exists.
signals.example: SW-114 Conveyor Jam Clearing rev C - or - no written procedure exists for this task

questions.prompt: Was it being done as written?
What differed, and why?
questions.help: Not about blame. A method people cannot follow is a finding about the method.
questions.why: A recorded deviation with its reason is the most actionable single sentence a description can contain.
questions.placeholder: Example: the interlock was bypassed with a spare key because a full stop needs a fifteen minute restart
examples: The guard interlock was bypassed with a spare key because clearing the jam through the access door takes about fifteen minutes and the line was down
The procedure calls for a two-person lift but only one person was on shift at that hour

questions.prompt: What PPE was being worn?
questions.help: Tick everything that was actually on at the time.

questions.prompt: Was that the specified PPE for this task?
What was the equipment or tool?
questions.help: Asset number or line and station if you have it, otherwise the type.
questions.why: Equipment detail is missing from 87.3 percent of past descriptions. A reviewer cannot check whether other units share the hazard without knowing which unit this was.
questions.placeholder: Example: infeed conveyor CV-04 at station 4
examples: Infeed conveyor CV-04 at station 4
Manual guillotine shear, asset 11872
Utility knife with a retractable blade

questions.prompt: What state was it in?
questions.help: Tick every state that applied at the moment.

questions.prompt: What condition was it in?
Briefly, what was wrong with it?
questions.help: One line is enough.
questions.placeholder: Example: the blade was noted as dull in the shift log twice
examples: The blade was noted as dull in the shift log twice
The guard latch has been sticking for about a month

questions.prompt: How heavy was what was being handled?
What made it awkward, if anything?
questions.help: Tick anything that applied. Leave blank if it was an easy shape to handle.

questions.prompt: How was it being held?
Just before: what was happening?
questions.help: Where the person was standing relative to the equipment, and what each hand was doing.
questions.why: Basic sequence context is missing from 68.6 percent of past descriptions. Where someone was standing and what their hands were doing is usually what explains the injury.
questions.placeholder: Example: leaning over the conveyor side rail with the right arm inside the guard opening
examples: Leaning over the conveyor side rail with the right arm extended into the guard opening and the left hand on the rail
Squatting beside the pallet with the load at floor level, back turned toward the mixer platform
Walking at normal pace along the main aisle carrying a wrench and looking ahead

questions.prompt: Which figure is closest to the body position at that moment?
questions.help: Pick the nearest one. It does not have to be exact.
questions.why: Bent over covers a squat, a stoop and a twist, which are three different mechanisms. A picture takes a second and gives a reviewer something a sentence usually does not.

questions.prompt: The moment: what happened, in order?
questions.help: What moved first, what happened next, and where the injury came in that order.
questions.why: This is the sentence reviewers most need and least often get. Back injury from lifting is a conclusion, not a description.
questions.placeholder: Example: the carton released, the belt restarted, and the right hand was pulled against the guard edge
examples: The carton released suddenly, the belt restarted under its own control logic, and the right hand was pulled against the fixed edge of the guard opening
The load shifted left as it cleared the pallet, the torso twisted left to keep hold of it, and a sharp pain was felt across the lower back
The right foot contacted hydraulic fluid, slid forward, and the fall was taken onto the right hip

signals.message: That tells us the outcome. What was the motion? Describe what moved and in what direction.
signals.example: The load shifted left as it cleared the pallet and the torso twisted left to keep hold of it.

questions.prompt: Straight after: what did the person and the equipment do?
questions.help: The first few seconds. Did the machine keep running, stop, or trip.
questions.placeholder: Example: the hand was withdrawn, the conveyor kept running, and the team lead was called
examples: The hand was withdrawn, the conveyor kept running, and the team lead was called from the station intercom
The load was set down, the employee stayed standing holding the lower back, and work at the station stopped

questions.prompt: What was the prior condition related to?
What changed about the condition?
questions.help: The difference in symptoms or function, and the activity that coincided with it.
questions.why: For an aggravation the case turns on what got worse and what work was being done when it did. Without both, the record cannot support a recordability decision either way.
questions.placeholder: Example: previously intermittent, now constant and radiating into the right leg after the lift
examples: The lower back symptoms had been intermittent for two years. After lifting the resin bag the pain became constant and radiated into the right leg
The repaired right shoulder had full range of motion until the pull on the jammed lever, after which the arm could not be raised above shoulder height

questions.prompt: How and when was it noticed?
questions.help: What was first observed, and roughly when.
questions.placeholder: Example: a rash across both forearms noticed at the end of shift while washing up
examples: A rash across both forearms was noticed at the end of the shift while washing up
A hearing shift was identified at the annual audiometric test

questions.prompt: Over what period could the exposure have happened, doing what?
questions.placeholder: Example: the two shifts before, both spent decanting solvent without sleeve protection
examples: The two shifts before, both spent decanting solvent at the parts washer without sleeve protection
The last four months on the press line, where hearing protection is required but not consistently worn

questions.prompt: How often is this task done?
How long has this person been doing it?
questions.help: On this specific task, not their total service.

questions.prompt: Describe one cycle of the task.
questions.help: A single repetition from start to finish, including the motions.
questions.why: For a cumulative case, one cycle described well is worth more than any amount of general description. It is the unit the exposure is made of.
questions.placeholder: Example: reach 20 inches to the bin, grasp the part, rotate the wrist to seat it, press down, release
examples: Reach forward about 20 inches into the bin, grasp the part, rotate the right wrist to seat it in the fixture, press down with the heel of the hand, release and return
Lift a tray from waist height to a shelf at shoulder height with both arms extended, hold it while the label is applied, then lower it

signals.message: Describe the motions - what the arms, hands and back actually do.
signals.example: Reach forward about 20 inches, grasp the part, rotate the wrist to seat it, press down with the heel of the hand.

questions.prompt: Which figure is closest to the posture held during the task?
questions.help: Pick the nearest one.

questions.prompt: How much force does it take?
When did symptoms start, and what were they?
questions.help: Approximate timing is fine.
questions.placeholder: Example: aching in the right wrist about six weeks ago, at first only at the end of a shift
examples: Aching in the right wrist first noticed about six weeks ago, at first only towards the end of a shift
Tightness across the right shoulder starting roughly two months ago, noticed on waking

questions.prompt: How have they changed since?
What has changed in this work recently?
questions.help: Rate, method, tooling, materials, staffing, layout. If nothing changed, say so - that is also a finding.
questions.why: For cumulative cases the cause is usually a change in exposure, not the task itself. This is the closest a description gets to a cause.
questions.placeholder: Example: the line rate went from 220 to 300 per shift a month ago when a station was removed
examples: The line rate increased from 220 to 300 units per shift about a month ago when the second station was removed
The fixture was replaced six weeks ago and the new one sits about 4 inches further forward
Nothing about the task has changed in the last year

questions.prompt: What moved, and what did it move against?
questions.help: Name both. In a struck-by the object moves; in a struck-against the person moves.
questions.placeholder: Example: a 6 foot length of bar stock slid off the rack and fell onto the left shoulder
examples: A 6 foot length of steel bar stock slid off the top of the rack and fell onto the left shoulder
The employee straightened up quickly and the top of the head struck the fixed conveyor frame

questions.prompt: How far did it travel?
How heavy was the object?
What two surfaces was the body part caught between?
questions.help: Name both, including which one moved.
questions.placeholder: Example: between the moving belt and the fixed steel edge of the guard opening
examples: Between the moving conveyor belt and the fixed steel edge of the guard opening
Between the descending press ram and the fixed lower die

questions.prompt: How did the body part get into that zone?
questions.help: Reaching in, guard removed, hand following material, pulled in. Be specific about the opening.
questions.why: How the body part got into the danger zone is usually where the control failed. It is the most useful sentence in a caught-in case.
questions.placeholder: Example: reaching through a 5 inch gap in the guard to free the carton without stopping the belt
examples: The right hand was reaching through a 5 inch gap in the guard to free the jammed carton without stopping the belt
The guard had been removed for the changeover and not refitted before the machine was cycled

questions.prompt: What released it?
How heavy was the load?
It moved from
and moved to
How far from the body was it held?
questions.help: A load held close is a different exposure from the same load at arm reach.

questions.prompt: What about a lifting aid?
questions.why: Whether a control existed and went unused is a different corrective action from no control existing at all.

questions.prompt: One person or a team lift?
How was the team lift coordinated, and what went wrong?
questions.placeholder: Example: the near end was raised a second early and the load tipped toward the injured employee
examples: The lift was called by the other handler, the far end was raised about a second early, and the load tipped toward the injured employee
Both ends were raised together and the load stayed level throughout

questions.prompt: What was the walking surface?
What was on it or wrong with it?
questions.help: Tick everything that applied.

questions.prompt: What did the foot do, and how was the fall taken?
questions.help: Slip, trip or misstep, which foot, and what part of the body landed first.
questions.placeholder: Example: the right foot slid forward on the fluid and the fall was taken onto the right hip
examples: The right foot slid forward on the fluid, balance was lost backwards, and the fall was taken onto the right hip and the outstretched right hand
The left toe caught the raised weld seam, the body pitched forward, and both knees contacted the decking first

questions.prompt: What footwear was being worn?
How far was the fall?
What was being worked from, and what was landed on?
questions.help: Ladder, platform, scaffold, vehicle, roof. Include whether it was set up correctly.
questions.placeholder: Example: an 8 foot stepladder with one leg on a cable tray, landing on sealed concrete
examples: An 8 foot fiberglass stepladder set on a slight slope with one leg on a cable tray, landing on sealed concrete
A scissor lift platform at about 12 feet, landing on the platform deck itself

questions.prompt: Was fall protection required?
questions.why: Required, available and in use are three separate facts and frequently three different answers. A reviewer needs all three.

questions.prompt: Was it available at the location?
Was it actually being used?
What started the fall?
questions.help: Overreach, ladder shift, missed step, surface failure, loss of grip.
questions.placeholder: Example: the ladder shifted left as the reach extended past the side rail
examples: The ladder shifted to the left as the employee reached out past the side rail toward the valve
The right foot missed the second step on the way down while carrying a part in one hand

questions.prompt: What is the motion, precisely?
questions.help: Which joint, in what direction, through roughly what range.
questions.placeholder: Example: right wrist rotation of about 90 degrees with the wrist bent back
examples: Right wrist rotation of about 90 degrees with the wrist bent back, combined with a downward press using the heel of the hand
Repeated overhead reach with the right arm above shoulder height and the elbow extended

questions.prompt: How often is it repeated?
How much force per repetition?
What was the substance or energy, and where did it come from?
questions.placeholder: Example: heated caustic wash solution from the parts washer transfer line
examples: Heated caustic wash solution from the parts washer transfer line at the quick disconnect fitting
The heated platen of the laminating press
A 480 volt supply at the disconnect switch inside the panel

questions.prompt: Temperature, voltage or concentration?
questions.help: Approximate is fine. If it is not known, use I do not know rather than guessing.
questions.placeholder: Example: about 180 degrees Fahrenheit, roughly 4 percent caustic
examples: About 180 degrees Fahrenheit, roughly 4 percent caustic
480 volts, three phase

questions.prompt: How long was the contact?
What was the isolation state of the source?
questions.help: Tick everything that applied.
questions.why: For energy contact cases the isolation state is the control that either held or did not. It is the first thing an investigator looks for.

questions.prompt: What was the agent, and where was it coming from?
questions.placeholder: Example: welding fume from stainless MIG welding at the fabrication bench
examples: Welding fume from stainless steel MIG welding at the fabrication bench
Solvent vapour from the open parts washer tank
Continuous noise from the press line at the adjacent station

questions.prompt: How long was the exposure?
What ventilation or engineering control was in place?
Describe the vehicle movement and the point of impact.
questions.help: What vehicle, who was operating it by role, direction and rough speed, and what was struck.
questions.placeholder: Example: a counterbalance forklift reversing at walking pace struck the left foot of a pedestrian
examples: A sit down counterbalance forklift reversing at about walking pace struck the left foot of a pedestrian at the aisle intersection
The pallet truck rolled forward on the dock slope and pinned the right ankle against the dock plate

questions.prompt: Describe the physical mechanism in full.
questions.help: Because the accident type is other, this answer carries the whole mechanism.
questions.why: Other means no branch of tailored questions applies, so the bar for this single answer is higher than usual.
questions.placeholder: What moved, in what direction, with what force, and how the body was loaded
examples: While seated at the inspection bench the chair gas cylinder collapsed, dropping the seat about 5 inches, and the lower back was compressed against the seat back

questions.prompt: Which direction did the force come from?
Where exactly on the body?
questions.help: Be specific about side and location. The form has the body part; this is the precise spot.
questions.why: This is what makes a description medically useful. Hand injury and a laceration across the base of the right index finger are not the same record.
questions.placeholder: Example: back of the right hand at the base of the index and middle fingers
examples: Back of the right hand at the base of the index and middle fingers
Outer left forearm, about 4 inches below the elbow
Lower back on the left side

questions.prompt: What was different from a normal run of this task?
questions.help: Anything at all. If genuinely nothing was different, say that plainly.
questions.why: Root cause information is missing from 90.7 percent of past descriptions, the largest gap in the data. This one question closes more of it than any other. Nothing was different is a legitimate answer.
questions.placeholder: Example: the jam happened three times that shift instead of once a week, on a new supplier carton
examples: The jam occurred three times that shift where it normally happens about once a week, and the line had been running cartons from a new supplier since Monday
The regular operator was on leave and this was a first shift on the station for a covering employee
Nothing was different. This is the task as it is normally performed

questions.prompt: What conditions applied at that spot?
questions.help: Tick everything. Pick nothing notable if the environment played no part.

questions.prompt: Briefly, what were those conditions like?
questions.help: One line, enough that someone who was not there can picture the spot.
questions.placeholder: Example: the aisle light above the station has been out for about two weeks
examples: The aisle light above the station has been out for about two weeks
The floor at the transfer point is routinely damp from the washer with no drain nearby

questions.prompt: How far into the shift?
questions.why: Time into shift and overtime are among the few fatigue signals a description can carry, and they are almost never recorded.

questions.prompt: Was overtime being worked?
How far into this task?
First time doing this task?
Was there a known hazard, prior near miss or open action covering this task?
What was already known?
questions.help: Reference the near miss, action or assessment if you can.
questions.why: A description that records a prior near miss on the same hazard changes how the case is reviewed and how fast it is acted on.
questions.placeholder: Example: a near miss was raised four months ago for the same guard opening and the action is still open
examples: A near miss was raised about four months ago for reaching into the same guard opening, and the corrective action to fit a fixed shield is still open
The task is covered by risk assessment RA-318, which identifies manual handling of the bags as a medium risk

questions.prompt: Was a guard, interlock or control bypassed, missing or ineffective?
Which control, and in what way?
questions.placeholder: Example: the belt guard has a 5 inch service opening that allows a hand to reach the roller
examples: The belt guard has a 5 inch service opening that allows a hand to reach the return roller while the belt is running
The interlock on the access door had been bypassed with a spare key kept at the station

questions.prompt: Could the work have been stopped, and what made stopping hard?
questions.help: Not about blame. If a stop-work point existed and was not taken, the reason is the finding.
questions.why: Where stop-work authority is not used the reason is usually structural - a rate target, no cover, an approval that takes too long. That reason is what a corrective action has to change.
questions.placeholder: Example: the belt could have been stopped but a restart takes fifteen minutes and the line was behind
examples: The belt could have been stopped to clear the jam, but a full stop needs a restart sequence taking about fifteen minutes and the line was already behind
There was no point at which stopping would have changed the outcome
The work was stopped as soon as the condition was noticed

questions.prompt: What was done at the scene?
questions.help: Tick everything that was given.
questions.why: Immediate action is missing from 82.0 percent of past descriptions. What was applied affects the clinical picture and the first-aid versus medical-treatment recordability decision.

questions.prompt: Anything else about the treatment?
questions.help: Optional. Duration, or what was applied where.
questions.placeholder: Example: irrigated for about 15 minutes at the eyewash station
examples: Irrigated for about 15 minutes at the eyewash station
Cold pack held on the lower back for about 20 minutes

not.equals: no first aid was given at the scene

questions.prompt: Who gave it?
questions.help: By role. Never a name.

questions.prompt: Was the employee sent for evaluation?
questions.help: Provider type only. The facility name and address belong on the form.

questions.prompt: Who was told?
questions.help: Tick everyone notified.

questions.prompt: How soon after the event?
Why was the report delayed?
questions.help: State it plainly. Mild at first, busy shift, hoped it would settle. All real, none a problem to record.
questions.why: A delayed report with a stated reason is a stronger record than one with a silence where the reason should be. Reporting friction is itself a finding.
questions.placeholder: Example: the discomfort was mild and was expected to settle overnight
examples: The discomfort was mild at the time and was expected to settle overnight. It was worse the following morning
The line was short staffed and the employee did not want to stop the run

in: at the end of the shift

questions.prompt: What was done with the area and the equipment?
questions.help: Tick everything that was done.

questions.prompt: What happened to the work afterwards?

formChecklist.label: Case date, reported date and time, shift and shift start time
Employee name, occupation, department, SSO, supervisor, contingent or temp status
formChecklist.note: None of this belongs in the description text.

formChecklist.label: Equipment selected from the structured picker
PSE determination, Injury vs Illness, Site Case number, privacy case flag
OSHA recordability and the recordability rationale
Place of accident or exposure, on-premises flag, incident location, workstation, GPS
Process safety incident flag, associated cases, related customers
Life Saving Rule or Rules selected
Case Severity level A to E
Accident Type, Principal Body Part and Detailed Body Parts
Object or substance which directly injured or exposed the employee
Physician or treatment facility name and address, ER treatment, overnight hospitalization
